title: Shakshuka Poached Eggs Tomato

seo.title: Authentic Shakshuka Recipe: Easy Poached Eggs in Tomato Sauce
seo.metaDescription: Master the art of Shakshuka with our easy, authentic Middle Eastern recipe. Perfect poached eggs simmered in a rich tomato sauce. A delicious breakfast!
seo.h1: Authentic Shakshuka Recipe: Poached Eggs in Spicy Tomato Sauce
seo.imageAlt: Close-up of a skillet of authentic shakshuka with perfectly poached eggs in a rich tomato sauce, garnished with fresh herbs.
seo.imageCaption: Our authentic shakshuka recipe brings the vibrant flavors of the Middle East to your breakfast table, featuring perfectly poached eggs.

description: Shakshuka is a vibrant and beloved Middle Eastern breakfast dish featuring eggs gently poached in a rich, spiced tomato and bell pepper sauce. This comforting one-pan meal is brimming with aromatic flavors and is perfect for sharing with family and friends. Enjoy the warm, hearty taste of tradition with every delicious bite.

instructions.title: Prepare Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep skillet or cast-iron pan over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Bell Peppers
instructions.text: Stir in the diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peppers begin to soften but still retain a slight crispness. This adds a wonderful texture to the sauce.

instructions.title: Introduce Spices
instructions.text: Add the ground cumin, paprika, and chili powder to the skillet. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the spices are fragrant. This step helps to bloom the spices and deepen their flavor.

instructions.title: Simmer Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and water or vegetable broth. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it cook for 10-15 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully.

instructions.title: Create Wells for Eggs
instructions.text: Once the sauce has thickened slightly and the flavors have developed, taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed. Using the back of a spoon, create four shallow wells or indentations in the tomato sauce for the eggs.

instructions.title: Poach the Eggs
instructions.text: Carefully crack one egg into each well. You can crack them into a small bowl first to ensure no shell gets into the pan. Cover the skillet again and continue to cook for 5-8 minutes, or until the egg whites are set and the yolks are still runny, or cooked to your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the skillet from the heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley or cilantro. Serve immediately, directly from the skillet, with warm pita bread or crusty bread for dipping into the delicious sauce and runny yolks.

tips: To achieve perfectly runny yolks, ensure the heat is low when poaching the eggs and watch them carefully. Remove from heat as soon as the whites are set.
For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of smoked paprika or a small amount of harissa paste along with the other spices.
Shakshuka is best served hot, directly from the pan. Pair it with warm pita bread, challah, or crusty sourdough for soaking up the rich tomato sauce.
